text:
kai: quick proposal: add per-route redact_profile with three presets (minimal, debug_strip, full_scrub) + tenant-tier default. goal: reduce noisy manual flags and make routing cost-aware. thoughts?

rebecca: love the presets. we need clear definitions though. e.g. minimal = headers + first 128 chars, debug_strip = headers + structured fields, full_scrub = remove user text + attachments hashed.

omar: operational concern: how do we surface when `debug_strip` prevents reproducing incidents? need a metric to tie truncation -> investigation failures.

jena: propose metrics: `route.redact.truncated_count`, `route.redact.blocked_debugs_count`, and `route.redact.post_trim_token_estimate_sum`. also a histogram `route.redact.post_trim_size_bytes`.

li: product asks whether tenant-tier default should be automatic (e.g., startup tier = minimal, enterprise = debug_strip) or require opt-in. my vote: sensible default by tier + tenant admin override.

kai: agree. example route config sketch: 
```yaml
routes:
  - id: /v1/generate
    redact_profile: debug_strip  # minimal|debug_strip|full_scrub
    sampling_hint: 0.02
    quota_behavior: respect
```
we also surface `sampling_hint` so Optimize can suggest a replay/sampling plan.

rebecca: about attachments: we should canonicalize to `signature=mime/len/hmac` and never store raw base64. code sketch: 
```py
def attachment_signature(b64, salt):
    mime = guess_mime(b64)
    return hmac_sha256(salt, f"{mime}/{len(b64)}")
```
store: {signature:..., preview: false}
```

omar: RBAC + audit: changes to tenant default or route-level `redact_profile` must create an audit entry and be gated by org_admin or product_admin. support can request a temp override which creates a time-limited ticketed audit record.

jena: console UX: show redact pill + profile name on log rows. clicking shows a small modal with what was removed (counts, hashes, retained fields) and a CTA to open an `inspect` (requires inspector token). also surface an estimated cost delta (monthly projection) if tenant flips profile.

li: billing note: trimmed events should count differently. propose `debug_storage_units` vs `ingest_storage_units`. draft billing delta formula in RFC.

kai: rollout plan: feature flag `redact_profiles_v1` behind canary; deploy plan: canary on prod-2 (10% traffic) -> prod-1 (50%) -> global. opsbot will gate if `route.redact.blocked_debugs_count` > 100 in 1h.

auditbot: featureflag: redact_profiles_v1 enabled on prod-2 at 2026-04-05T18:00:00Z (canary 10%).

rebecca: test plan: unit tests for each preset, e2e with synthetic prompts that include emails/ssn, attachment fuzzing for mime detection, and integration with console rendering.

omar: edgecases: webhooks that sign payloads -> hashing will change signature. need a whitelist for passthrough attachments or a normalized signature algorithm that preserves verification. flagging to security.

jena: telemetry: we'll emit `redact_profile_applied` with labels route, tenant, profile, truncated(boolean), sample_hint. that'll allow dashboard pivoting.

li: legal: full_scrub must follow short retention policy by default and be marked for expedited deletion on request. include retention text in tenant policy UI.

kai: deployment owners: @omar for runtime patch, @jena for console, @rebecca for scrub logic, @li for billing/legal sync. i'll author RFC with config examples, permission model, and dashboards. will link here when ready.

rebecca: small UX follow-up: add a toggle in tenant settings: "Allow support temporary unredact" with TTL and automatic audit ticket creation.

omar: implemented fallback: if `redact_profile` prevents a must-have debug (based on SLI), router can request temporary `inspect_token` from ops via escalation flow. will log `inspect_request_{ok|denied}`.

jena: i'll add dashboard alert: `redact.blocked_debug_ratio > 0.05` for 30m -> page SRE.

li: noted. legal will draft required retention text and opt-out clauses.

auditbot: RFC created: https://go/internal/rfc/per-route-redact-profiles (DRAFT).

kai: great work. let's keep this lean and ship the basic presets first.
